label: Sixth-edition aphorisms
title: Aphorism § 48
text:
§ 48



 Neither in the course of nature, as we see from all the above
          examples, nor by the physician's art, can an existing affection or malady in any one
          instance be removed by a dissimilar morbific agent, be it ever so strong, but solely by
          one that is similar in symptoms and is somewhat stronger, according to eternal,
          irrevocable laws of nature, which have not hitherto been recognized.
